<!-- openab-council -->
CHANGES REQUESTED ⚠️ — the SHA-bound review authority and evaluator logic verify clean, but the released image and Python artifacts are not source-bound, and the PR description mischaracterizes new security-sensitive code as pre-existing.
Reviewed at db4c91f373a8fa69189a3fdeee3dc99e96891ee9 (round 1)

## What This PR Does
Binds PR-review/status authority to verified, controller-owned commit SHAs (reviews fail closed on malformed or mismatched SHAs) and adds an independently packaged offline model evaluator. The evaluator combines independent judgments, source-bound OCI validation, synthesis, discovery, and hash-verified weekly reporting, shipped as a Python package (`ocp-review-eval`, `ocp-review-weekly` v0.1.0) with a dedicated nonroot Docker image and an `evaluation-vX.Y.Z` release workflow.

## How It Works
- **Rust (`crates/github-pr-controller/src/`)**: `canonical_commit_id` canonicalizes SHAs (40-char lowercased hex, rejecting malformed/mismatched values); `enforce_authority_write` gates every write on `disposition == "verified"` plus a matching `commit_id` and controller marker, rejecting `legacy_unverified` rows. Postgres and SQLite stores keep parity on integrity columns/transactions and use bound parameters throughout.
- **Python evaluator (`scripts/review_model_*.py`, `review_round_weekly_report.py`)**: OCI executor and weekly report fail closed (raise/abort) on hash/digest mismatches rather than logging silently.
- **Packaging (`Dockerfile.evaluation`, `packaging/evaluation/run.sh`, `.github/workflows/evaluation-release.yml`, `pyproject.toml`, `MANIFEST.in`)**: image runs as nonroot (`USER evaluator`, uid 65532) end-to-end; the launcher allowlists exactly three auth env vars and bind-mounts the repo read-only; the release workflow cross-checks the tag/version against `pyproject.toml`.
- The remaining ~480 changed files are generated `.agentflow/` evaluation evidence, not reviewable logic.

## Findings

| ID  | Severity | Finding                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              | Location                                    |
| --- | -------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------- |
| F1  | 🟡       | All three build stages pull mutable image tags; a tag retarget or upstream compromise silently changes the published evaluator for the same source (raised by: rev-codex)                                                                            | Dockerfile.evaluation:2                     |
| F2  | 🟡       | Release job installs unpinned/ranged build + setuptools>=77 from PyPI, then builds the write-published wheel/sdist — resolution can drift between identical tag builds (raised by: rev-codex)                                                        | .github/workflows/evaluation-release.yml:87 |
| F3  | 🟡       | PR body calls the four evaluator modules "existing … unchanged by packaging," but none exist on base main — they are new security-sensitive code (OCI sandbox exec, hash verification), and the claim invites under-scrutiny (raised by: rev-claude) | PR description                              |
| F4  | 🟢       | PR body claims "42 artifact hashes and mtimes preserved," but this file has no os.utime/st_mtime preservation (only fromtimestamp for week bucketing); claim unsupported here, low impact (raised by: rev-claude)                                    | scripts/review_round_weekly_report.py       |

<details>
<summary>Finding Details</summary>

### 🟡 F1: Docker build stages use mutable image tags
`Dockerfile.evaluation` builds from `python:3.12-slim-bookworm` and `node:22-bookworm-slim` (×2) — all mutable tags. Because the published image is a security-sensitive evaluator that runs untrusted repository content, a tag retarget or a compromised upstream image can silently change what ships for the same source and release tag. Pin each `FROM` to an immutable `@sha256:` digest and bump it through an auditable dependency-update process. Confirmed: all three `FROM` lines at head use tags, no digests.

### 🟡 F2: Release workflow installs unpinned build backend
`.github/workflows/evaluation-release.yml` runs `pip install --disable-pip-version-check build setuptools>=77` from the default index, then uses that toolchain to produce the wheel/sdist published with write credentials. Dependency resolution can therefore differ between two builds of the same tag, so the released artifact is not reproducible from source. Install hash-pinned build requirements from a committed lock/constraints file. Confirmed at head (install line ~87).

### 🟡 F3: PR body mischaracterizes new modules as pre-existing
The description states "Its four existing evaluator modules remain unchanged by packaging." Fetching base `main` (`16aa2d4`) returns Not Found for all of `review_model_evaluation.py`, `review_model_adapters.py`, `review_model_oci_executor.py`, and `review_round_weekly_report.py` — they are introduced by this PR, not pre-existing. Under the claim-vs-behavior rule a shipped false claim is itself a defect: here it can cause reviewers to under-scrutinize newly added OCI-sandbox execution and hash-verification code. Fix: correct the PR description to describe these as new. Verified independently by the chair.

### 🟢 F4: Weekly-report mtime claim unsupported in this file
The PR body's "42 artifact hashes and mtimes preserved" is not backed by mtime-preservation logic in `review_round_weekly_report.py` — the only timestamp use is `datetime.fromtimestamp(...)` for ISO-week bucketing. Hash handling is present and fails closed; mtime preservation, if it exists, lives elsewhere. No code action required; correct or drop the claim if inaccurate. Green — documentation accuracy only, reviewer rated low with unconfirmed location.

</details>

<details>
<summary>What's Good (🟢)</summary>

- `canonical_commit_id` correctly canonicalizes to 40-char lowercased hex and rejects malformed/mismatched SHAs; formal-review response commit verification is enforced.
- `enforce_authority_write` gates every write on `verified` disposition + matching commit_id + controller marker, rejecting `legacy_unverified` rows; Postgres/SQLite parity maintained; SQL uses bound params throughout.
- `Dockerfile.evaluation` runs nonroot end-to-end (`USER evaluator` uid 65532 before ENTRYPOINT, no later root steps).
- `packaging/evaluation/run.sh` allowlists exactly three auth env vars and bind-mounts the repository read-only.
- OCI executor and weekly-report hash/digest mismatches fail closed (raise/abort), and the release workflow's tag regex + version cross-check against `pyproject.toml` (0.1.0) are correct.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Baseline Check</summary>

- Base `main` (`16aa2d4`) does not contain the four evaluator modules — they are net-new in this PR (verified by chair; basis for F3).
- Net-new value: SHA-bound review authority (fail-closed) + an independently packaged, nonroot, hash-verifying offline evaluator.
- CI/checks: pending, 0 contexts reported at head `db4c91f` — no CI signal available to the council.
- Scope note: 492 files changed but ~480 are generated `.agentflow/` evidence; review targeted the executable Rust/Python and packaging surfaces.
- No prior council verdict exists; this is a first-round review.
- Not verified by static review: the PR's "96 Python tests, no skips," isolated wheel/sdist install, and "130s fresh Linux evaluation" claims.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Review Metadata</summary>

- Reviewers: rev-codex (request changes — supply-chain/source-binding), rev-claude (request changes — correctness/claim verification, split on severity of docs findings).
- Consensus: **request changes**
- Absent reviewers: none

</details>

---
🔴×0 🟡×3 🟢×2 · 💬 Comment `@openab-council <question>` for a follow-up · 🔁 Push new commits or comment `@openab-council review <fix notes>` to re-run the council
